title: Open a sealed desiccator and take out the sample
instruction: Take the sample vial out of the desiccator and stand it on the white tray. Put the desiccator's lid on the grey pad, and do not move the desiccator itself.
context: Chemical technicians (O*NET 19-4031.00) open a desiccator by holding its base and sliding the greased ground-glass lid sideways: the seal and slight vacuum stop the lid lifting straight off, and a lid pushed alone drags the whole desiccator along the bench. One arm must hold the base while the other slides the lid.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Desiccator base: pale blue glass, 0.6 kg, 15 cm round flange with top 8 cm high, 14 cm body, two 3 cm square carrying lugs at y +-8.75 to 11.5 (3.5 cm tall), porcelain plate 1.5 cm high inside, centred x 29, y 0. Lid: glass, 0.4 kg, 15 cm flange 0.8 cm thick, 5.5 cm radius dome to 3.5 cm, dark 3.5 cm knob 3 cm tall (top 14.5 cm high). Vial: amber glass, 2.8 cm x 6 cm, 30 g, standing on the plate at x 29, y 0. Grey pad 17 x 17 cm at x 25, y -21; white tray 8 x 8 cm at x 23, y 17.
scoring: Measured with a ruler and protractor. 0 at any time if the desiccator slid more than 15 mm, rose more than 8 mm or turned 10 degrees, the vial tipped over 30 degrees, or the lid dropped (about 2.5 cm or more) or tilted over 45 degrees; never undone. Otherwise at the end: 1.0 the vial stands upright (within 10 degrees) on the tray and the lid rests flat on the pad, both grippers open and 3 cm or more from the vial, lid and desiccator, and all three still within 1 mm for 1 s; 0.75 the same but a gripper is near or open too little or something moves; 0.5 vial on the tray and let go, lid not on the pad; 0.25 lid off the desiccator (6 cm sideways or 1 cm up) but vial not on the tray.
reset_notes: Put the vial on the plate and the desiccator on its marked outline. Wipe and re-grease the flange thinly, seat the lid with a quarter twist, and draw the vacuum down to 2.6 kPa (20 mmHg) below room pressure through the lid's stopcock with a hand vacuum pump and gauge, then close the stopcock. Check with a spring scale before each trial: the lid slides at 6 to 7 N pulled sideways by its knob with the base held, and the sealed desiccator slides on the bench at 2 to 3 N. The pad and tray stay put.
fidelity: Rigid boxes and cylinders. A script models the seal: while the lid is within 4.5 cm of the base axis and seated it adds 40 N down on the lid and 40 N up on the base (lid slides at about 6.6 N, base at about 2.5 N); no contact force cap is enforced.
